condition: Concealed placental abruption after assault in pregnancy
permutationLabel: 33 weeks, pushed by partner, concealed abruption (no vaginal bleeding), fetal bradycardia
summary: 26-year-old at 33 weeks, "pushed by my partner" against a kitchen counter 3 h ago: constant abdominal pain, hard tender uterus, no vaginal bleeding, fetal heart 100/min, HR 112, BP 104/68, fibrinogen 1.6. Concealed abruption with fetal compromise; intimate-partner violence.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Abdominal pain after a fall, 33 weeks pregnant
inputs.hpi: Initially said she slipped. On private questioning: pushed by her partner and fell against the kitchen counter 3 hours ago, striking her abdomen. Constant severe abdominal pain since, uterus "hard", baby moving less. No vaginal bleeding or fluid loss. Previous bruises seen at antenatal visits. Blood group A RhD positive.

exam.general: Anxious, pale. HR 112, BP 104/68 (booking 122/78), RR 20. Old and new bruises on both upper arms.
exam.abdomen: Bruise over the upper abdomen. Uterus woody-hard and tender throughout, larger than dates. Fetal heart 100/min on Doppler. No vaginal bleeding on inspection.

inputs.socialHistory: Unemployed. Lives with partner. Disclosed previous episodes of violence.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Concealed placental abruption after abdominal trauma (partner assault) at 33 weeks
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Concealed placental abruption after blunt abdominal trauma from intimate-partner assault at 33 weeks: fetal bradycardia, early coagulopathy. Left lateral tilt, obstetric emergency team now, CTG, crossmatch and coagulation screen, anaesthetist; domestic-abuse safeguarding and safety plan.

redFlags.note: Disclosed intimate-partner violence in pregnancy: a safety issue for mother and baby.

mustInclude.note: NICE PH50: respond to disclosure with risk assessment, safety planning and referral.

mustExclude.note: An ACS, PE or AF antithrombotic/thrombolytic plan must never be attached to this diagnosis. Regression guard for DiagnosisRadiationEngine keyword matching: before 999f838 (word-boundary lookup) "mi" inside "abdominal" would have attached the ACS plan (aspirin 300 mg, ticagrelor, fondaparinux) to a placental abruption. With word-boundary matching no radiation entry matches (simulated from the source); to be confirmed on the first iOS CI run.

guideline.name: ATLS 10th edition — trauma in pregnancy
guideline.section: Chapter 12: resuscitate the mother first; manual uterine displacement / left lateral tilt after ~20 weeks; early obstetric consultation; cardiotocographic fetal monitoring after injury beyond viability; consider placental abruption (uterine tenderness, contractions, fetal distress, may be concealed); consider intimate partner violence
guideline.citation: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. ATLS Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: ACS; 2018. Chapter 12.

guideline.name: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 63 — antepartum haemorrhage
guideline.section: Placental abruption may be concealed (pain, tense tender uterus, fetal compromise without visible bleeding); maternal resuscitation; FBC, coagulation screen, crossmatch; CTG; delivery decisions by the obstetric team
guideline.citation: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists. Antepartum haemorrhage. Green-top Guideline No. 63. London: RCOG; 2011.

guideline.name: NICE PH50 — domestic violence and abuse: multi-agency working
guideline.section: Staff trained to ask about domestic violence and abuse in a safe, private setting and to respond with risk assessment, safety planning and referral to specialist services; pregnancy is a period of increased risk
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Domestic violence and abuse: multi-agency working. Public health guideline PH50, 2014.

rationale: Abruption can be concealed: pain, a tense tender uterus and fetal compromise without visible bleeding. Intimate-partner violence often starts or escalates in pregnancy and must be asked about and acted on.
